passages.original: Ecce spectaculum dignum ad quod respiciat intentus operi suo deus, ecce par deo dignum, vir fortis cum fortuna mala compositus, utique si et provocavit. Non video, inquam, quid habeat in terris Iuppiter pulchrius, si eo convertere animum velit, quam ut spectet Catonem iam partibus non semel fractis stantem nihilo minus inter ruinas publicas rectum.
passages.english: Behold a spectacle worthy of the regard of a god intent upon his own work; behold a pair worthy of a god: a brave man matched against evil fortune, especially if he has also challenged it. I do not see, I say, what Jupiter has on earth more beautiful, should he wish to turn his mind there, than to watch Cato, his party already broken more than once, standing nonetheless upright amid the public ruins.
passages.notes: "Compositus" is a gladiatorial term for a fighter paired against an opponent; "par" likewise means a matched pair of combatants. "Partibus" refers to Cato's political party or side in the civil wars.
